FINAL DELIVERABLE — EXPERIMENT DESIGN (written design only; NO experiment was run, no pilot executed, no results claimed)

Title: Training-set-size scaling of parametric surrogate models for aerodynamic drag (Cd) on DrivAerNet++ 26-parameter designs

1. RESEARCH QUESTION AND RATIONALE
Q1: Does surrogate predictive performance for drag (Cd) improve as training-set size n grows?
Q2: Does the improvement (scaling behavior) differ across model architectures?
Rationale: Parametric surrogates (inputs = 26 design parameters, output = Cd) are the cheap alternative to CFD, but their data-efficiency is architecture-dependent: classical low-bias models (trees, boosting) saturate early; high-capacity models (MLPs) need more data; GPs excel at small n but scale poorly computationally. A controlled learning-curve comparison isolates these effects.

2. DATA
- Source: DrivAerNet++ parametric design matrix (~8,000 car designs; fastback/notchback/estateback variants) with CFD drag coefficients Cd; feature vector = the 26 specified design parameters, one-hot encoded if any are categorical.
- ASSUMPTION (not verifiable here — network disabled, no local data): the dataset is publicly downloadable and Cd labels cover all three variants.
- Imbalance adaptation: if variant counts are imbalanced, (a) all splits are stratified proportional to the population (preserves real-world error estimates); (b) an OPTIONAL equal-variant balanced test subset is retained for subgroup comparison; (c) OPTIONAL per-variant subgroup analysis: learning curves per body type, run only if n_variant at the smallest ladder rung ≥ 128 (e.g., a variant with <~10% of designs supports only the larger rungs); otherwise report a per-variant error decomposition on the fixed test set only.

3. SPLIT PROTOCOL (internal validity over external comparability)
- One global split: 70% train pool (~5,600) / 15% validation (~1,200) / 15% test (~1,200), stratified by body type, drawn once with a fixed seed and reused for every model, every n, every seed. The test set is never touched by tuning or training.
- Training subsets at size n are drawn from the 70% train pool by k independent random subsamples (seeds s1..s5, reused identically across all architectures → paired comparisons).
- LIMITATION (explicit): this is OUR stratified split, not the official DrivAerNet++ train/test split; results are internally valid (same test set everywhere) but not directly comparable to published leaderboard numbers. Stated as a deviation.

4. TRAINING-SIZE LADDER
n_train ∈ {128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 5600} (≈ log-spaced, 7 points, ending at the full train-pool size).
Validation set fixed at full ~1,200 for all n. Test set fixed at ~1,200 for all n and all models.

5. MODEL ARCHITECTURE SET (all on the same 26 inputs, standardized using training-subset statistics only)
M1 Ridge regression (linear baseline).
M2 Ridge on fixed degree-2 polynomial features (modest parametric expansion; no data-driven feature selection so architecture, not feature engineering, is the differentiator).
M3 Random forest.
M4 Gradient-boosted trees (LightGBM/XGBoost).
M5 Exact Gaussian process, Matérn-5/2 + constant-mean, ARD lengthscales, standardized inputs. GP scalability treatment is EXPLICIT: exact GP only for n ≤ 2048; for n = 4096 and 5600 use a sparse/inducing-point variational GP (m = 512 inducing points, inducing set subsampled once per seed from the training subset). The n-cap and switch point are fixed a priori and reported alongside results (mixing exact and approximate GP is itself flagged as a caveat on the GP curve).
M6 MLP: 3 hidden layers × 128 units, ReLU, Adam, early stopping on validation RMSE, fixed epoch cap, deterministic seeds (CPU-only environment; this capacity is appropriate for 26-d inputs and avoids conflating scaling with GPU-scale model size).
M7 (sensitivity anchor) A second neural variant — wider MLP (4×256) — so that "architecture differences" can also be assessed within the neural family, not just between families.
Total: 7 architectures.

6. HYPERPARAMETER POLICY (per researcher decision: fixed, capped, per-size)
- For every (architecture, n, seed): random search with a FIXED BUDGET of 8 configurations drawn from a per-architecture search space that is IDENTICAL at every n (e.g., RF: max_depth ∈ {4,8,16,32,None}, min_samples_leaf ∈ {1,2,5,10}, n_estimators ∈ {100,300}; GBM: learning_rate ∈ {0.01,0.03,0.1}, num_leaves/depth, n_estimators ∈ {100,300,600}; MLP: lr ∈ {1e-4,3e-4,1e-3}, weight_decay, dropout; GP: lengthscale/nuiseance priors). Selection criterion: validation RMSE. Fixed budget + identical space at every n is the fairness device: small n cannot "win" by exhausting a bigger budget, and large n cannot be handicapped by a tiny one.
- Justification over frozen-at-max-n: hyperparameters optimal at n=5600 are typically too flexible or mis-regularized for n=128, so a frozen policy would depress small-n performance and exaggerate the apparent benefit of more data (steeper artificial slope). Conversely, unlimited per-size tuning could overfit the small validation sets at small n, making small-n look artificially good and flattening the curve (bias toward "no benefit"). The capped, size-invariant budget sits between these biases and keeps search effort constant, which is the quantity we hold fixed.
- MITIGATION / sensitivity check: for at least one architecture (M4, gradient boosting) report BOTH the tuned curve (capped per-size budget) and a frozen curve (best configuration selected once at n=5600, reused at all n). If the two slopes differ materially, that is reported as an explicit tuning-sensitivity result. Additionally report the validation-vs-test gap at each n per model as an overfitting-to-validation diagnostic.

7. METRICS
- Primary: RMSE of Cd on the fixed test set (per (model, n, seed)).
- Secondary: MAE, R², and normalized RMSE (RMSE / std of test Cd).
- Scaling metrics: per architecture, fit log(test RMSE) = a − b·log(n); b is the learning-rate exponent; compare b across architectures with bootstrap CIs.
- Cost metrics: wall-clock fit time and peak memory per fit (relevant especially to GP).

8. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS PLAN
- Learning curves: mean ± std over the 5 seeds per (model, n), same-subsample pairing across models.
- Main test: linear mixed model / two-way design on log(RMSE) with factors architecture and log(n) plus interaction; the interaction term directly answers Q2 (do scaling slopes differ?). Follow-up pairwise per-n comparisons between architectures using paired t-tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank across the 5 seed pairs, with Holm correction for the 21 pairwise architecture comparisons.
- Slope comparison: per-architecture b with bootstrap (resample seeds) 95% CIs; overlap/non-overlap of CIs reported alongside the mixed-model interaction.
- Effect framing: report RMSE ratios (e.g., RMSE at n=128 vs n=5600 per model) in addition to p-values.

9. CONTROLS
- Identical splits, subsample seeds, and standardization (fit on training subset only) across all models.
- Fixed early-stopping rule and epoch cap for MLPs; identical tree counts budget for RF/GBM search space; inducing-point count fixed for sparse GP.
- Environment pinning (library versions recorded); single-thread settings documented per library for reproducibility, with seeds parallelized across the 224 CPU cores.
- No test-set access during any tuning or model selection.

10. FEASIBILITY / RESOURCE ESTIMATE (estimate only — nothing was run)
Rough per-fit wall-clock on the CPU-only environment (single fit, one core-class job; 224 cores available to parallelize seeds/configs):
| Model | n=128 | n=1024 | n=4096–5600 |
| Ridge / poly-ridge | <0.1 s | <0.1 s | <0.5 s |
| RF (300 trees) | ~1–5 s | ~10–30 s | ~1–3 min |
| GBM | ~1–5 s | ~10–30 s | ~1–3 min |
| Exact GP | seconds | ~1–5 min | n/a (capped at 2048) |
| Sparse GP (m=512) | ~seconds | ~1–5 min | ~10–40 min |
| MLP (CPU) | ~1–2 min | ~5–10 min | ~15–30 min |
Total fits: 7 models × 7 sizes × 5 seeds = 245 final fits, plus tuning ≈ 245 × 8 = 1,960 candidate fits (many trivial). Optimistic aggregate ≈ 20–60 CPU-hours; pessimistic (sparse-GP and MLP tuning dominating) ≈ 150–300 CPU-hours. With ~200 usable cores this is on the order of 1–2 wall-clock days in the pessimistic case — feasible but not trivial, hence the fallback below.
- Seed policy: DEFAULT 5 seeds per (model, n). Documented fallback: if the pessimistic estimate is confirmed (e.g., sparse-GP tuning exceeding ~1 h per config), reduce to 3 seeds AND/OR reduce the tuning budget to 4 configurations for the two neural and GP models only; the reduction is applied uniformly across architectures and reported. Any fallback decision is recorded before unblinded results are examined.

11. INTERPRETATION CAVEATS
- CFD label-noise plateau: Cd labels carry finite-mesh/numerical noise; learning curves may plateau at a noise floor set by label quality rather than model capacity. We cannot estimate this floor without mesh-level metadata; small-n-vs-large-n gaps may therefore understate true model differences. Stated as an interpretation caveat, not measured.
- GP curve mixes exact (n≤2048) and sparse (n>2048) formulations; slope discontinuities near the switch point are attributed with that caveat.
- Tuning-policy sensitivity (Section 6) bounds but does not eliminate hyperparameter-driven slope bias.
- Scaling claims are bounded by the available data range (n ≤ ~5,600); extrapolation to much larger n is out of scope.
- Deviation from the official DrivAerNet++ split (Section 3).
- CPU-only training limits neural-model scale; conclusions about "neural architectures" apply to MLPs of this class on 26-d inputs, not to large deep models.

12. PSEUDOCODE OUTLINE
```
load parametric matrix X (N≈8000 × 26) and Cd y
stratified_split(X, y, by=variant) -> train_pool, val, test      # fixed seed, once
for n in [128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 5600]:
    for s in seeds[1..5]:                                        # default 5, fallback 3
        subset = subsample(train_pool, n, seed=s)                # same subsets reused by all models
        for model in [ridge, poly_ridge, rf, gbm, gp, mlp, wide_mlp]:
            candidates = random_search(model.space, budget=8)    # identical space at every n
            best = argmin_val_rmse(fit(candidates, subset, val)) # standardize on subset only
            test_rmse[model, n, s] = evaluate(best, test)
            log fit_time, peak_memory
# frozen sensitivity curve (M4 only):
best_5600 = argmin over tuning at n=5600; evaluate best_5600 (retrained on each subset) at all n
analyze: learning curves, log-log slopes + bootstrap CIs,
         mixed model log(RMSE) ~ architecture * log(n),
         paired per-n tests (Holm-corrected), val-vs-test gaps
```

13. STATEMENT
This is a design only. No code was written against data, no dataset was downloaded, no pilot or full run was executed, and no numerical results are claimed. All figures in Section 10 are feasibility estimates, not measurements.

Assumptions (distinct from fixed task requirements): DrivAerNet++ availability with Cd labels for all variants; 26 parameters form a fixed numeric vector (categoricals one-hot); CPU-only compute is sufficient per Section 10; preprocessing limited to standardization/one-hot so architecture is the differentiator. Fixed by the task: 26-parameter DrivAerNet++ inputs, Cd target, design-only scope, the researcher decisions in items (1)–(6) of your instruction.

Q1: Does surrogate predictive performance for drag (Cd) improve as training-set size n grows?
